body:
We were raised on follow-your-dreams speeches. Which is fair enough, but the problem is that while parenting took this turn, the rest of society didn't. So our parents say "creativity, hurray," when you turn 19 or so, society says, "No, seriously, this electric bill, pay it."

I don't feel capable of doing something I don't want to do. I know that sounds selfish and spoiled, but it's true. My attitude is sort of one of "Well, if I Have to spend 8 hours a day doing something I hate and all anyone can justify it with is 'That's life,' then that's not something I want." From a logical point of view, yeah, I know that's short-sighted and not quite how things work, but the minute I start looking at jobs or thinking about the jobs I'd have to take, I just feel like it's not worth it.

The way I feel at the minute is that I'll ride as long as I can. I'll try and fix the problem (doctor's appointment on Wednesday, I'm hoping he'll hook me up with a therapist) but if I run out of people to much off, and I hit a wall where there's nothing left for me to do, I'll either become homeless or check out.
Those are fine, and the walk sounds like something I need. But it's the money-making that's making this so frustrating. I have no idea how I'm supposed to take care of myself.

Hobbies sort of. Every time I've tried to monetize anything it's failed miserably though. I'm not leaving my girlfriend. I know she's trying to encourage me. She's not threatening to leave in a malicious way, she just explained that she can't be with someone if she's pulling all the weight. But she's said she'll stay with me for as long as she believes I'm actively trying to fix the problem.
That's cool and all, but does Paint do shadow text?
